_README.purpose: Stage 6 blocklists. DATA, not code (Prompt H): adding a banned word after this ships is a content change Reyner can approve, with no code deploy.
_README.how_to_edit: Every entry is { pattern, note }. `pattern` is a JavaScript regex SOURCE string, matched case-insensitively against rendered text only. Escape backslashes for JSON. tests/stage6-validation.spec.mjs compiles every pattern, so a malformed edit fails CI rather than production.
_README.scope: Matched against block text, block headings and penutup. NEVER against fact_ids, which legitimately carry hanzi (badge_桃花), and never against the semantic JSON.
_README.authority: Reyner is the sole authority on Indonesian register. Every note here explains why a pattern exists so a later reader can judge whether it still should.
_README.false_positives: Prefer a tight pattern that misses over a loose one that rejects real readings. A hard reject costs a regeneration; the measurement harness reports per-check rejection rates so an over-eager pattern is visible as a number.

hedge_construction.note: THE load-bearing regex. renderer-prompt-notes: CONFIRMED UNFIXABLE BY PROMPT ALONE - run 5 emitted it twice against an explicit ban, and gate-check run 2 emitted it a third time, in the penutup. This regex is the only reliable fix. The 140-char window keeps it inside one sentence; the lazy quantifier stops it spanning a whole paragraph. THE `bukan berarti` CARVE-OUT (Reyner, 2026-08-06, ruling A on the rejection gallery): the gallery showed this check's most common trigger was 'Lemah di sini bukan berarti tidak mampu, melainkan sumber tenagamu ada di luar dirimu' - which is the resolve-in-the-same-breath move rule 21 REQUIRES, not the hedge the ban was written for. 'bukan berarti X' NEGATES A MISREADING, which is the job; 'bukan X tapi Y' substitutes one claim for another, which is the hedge. The lookahead separates them, so the ban keeps catching what it was built for.

meta.note: renderer-prompt bans meta. The \b after AI is load-bearing: without it this pattern matches "Sebagai Air (Water)", which is correct prose on every Water chart. Same class of error as bare_polarity matching the pronoun `yang`.

The same self-identification as `sebagai AI` with the noun spelled out. Reyner's 2026-08-02 blind-judging notes list mid-reading system disclaimers as a defect class; this is its plainest form.

The safety disclaimer. Rule 25 is enforced by NOT giving medical or financial advice, which forbidden_content already hard-rejects; appending a disclaimer instead is the model covering itself inside a reading that should never have needed one.
A labelled aside. The reading has no apparatus - no notes, no footnotes, no caveats block. The colon is required so the ordinary noun `catatan` in prose does not match.

code_leak.note: A snake_case identifier: `label_meaning`, `fact_id`, `positions_id`, `support_share`. Reyner's 2026-08-02 blind-judging notes list raw variable/code-string leaks as a defect class. Indonesian prose contains no underscores, so this cannot fire on real copy. fact_ids are out of scope by construction (blocklist scope note) - they are excluded from the checked text.

camelCase: `supportShare`, `positionsId`, `factIds`. CASE-SENSITIVE, and that is load-bearing for the same reason bare_polarity is: under the default case-insensitive flags this pattern is `[a-z]+[a-z]` and matches EVERY word of two letters or more. Caught by the engine-string test on first run - it flagged all 398 glossary strings. Verified against the whole glossary and all 32 gate-passed samples from the 2026-08-02 pairs file: zero matches with the `u` flag.
Braces, square brackets, backticks and template-literal syntax. Parentheses are DELIBERATELY absent: rule 23 sanctions the English bracket, so banning ( ) would reject every correct reading.
A JSON key. The model echoing its own input structure into the prose.
A missing value rendered as its literal. The hour pillar is absent for a large share of users and `palaceName` returns null for it, so `Pilar null` is a reachable output and not a hypothetical.
The one payload field name that is a bare English word rather than snake_case, so nothing above catches it. Observed as a category in the notes; named explicitly for that reason.

arithmetic.note: renderer-prompt PROVENANCE IS NOT ARITHMETIC: never a percentage. Golden rule 1, hide the arithmetic.

raw_pillar.note: The raw pillar where a palace name belongs. renderer-prompt §THE PALACES AND THE PARTS bans it in as many words ('Do not downgrade it to "pilar hari"') and every one of the four pillars HAS a palace name, so the raw form is never needed. Added 2026-08-06 together with the fix to the prompt line that used to contradict the ban: §PROVENANCE IS NOT ARITHMETIC listed 'ini datang dari pilar harimu' as ENCOURAGED, which is what the renderer was following when it wrote 'Fondasi Pasanganmu berada di pilar hari' on chart 5. The contradiction is resolved first and this enforces the surviving rule, the same pairing as the 8-sentence paragraph rule. Pre-checked: zero matches against every rendered glossary field, and clean on all four 'Pilar X' palace names, which are capital-P and never followed by a pillar word. The \w* tail catches the possessive ('pilar harimu').

bare_polarity.note: Golden rule 5, NO BARE YIN/YANG. CASE-SENSITIVE, and that is load-bearing: "yang" is the ordinary Indonesian relative pronoun, so a case-insensitive version of this pattern matches "api yang menyala" and "Air yang terlalu banyak" and rejects correct prose. Measured 2026-08-02: it fired 20 times in the first live batch, all false positives.

_rule: EDITING THIS FILE CHANGES WHAT THE GATE REJECTS, SO IT BUMPS STAGE6_VERSION in lib/validate/index.js IN THE SAME COMMIT. Adding a pattern, removing one, moving one into a function - all of them. There is no edit here too small to move the number: the two entries in _removed below are one deletion and one move, and they left 1.9.0 stamped on two different gates for a day. Read the docblock on STAGE6_VERSION before you commit.

_removed.style.adverbial: DELETED 2026-08-17 (Reyner, on the 2026-08-18 rejection gallery). Was a token ban for a CONSTRUCTION defect. Measured over 40 runs: 14 findings, 9 of them the plain adverb secara konsisten, and NOT ONE was the construction the ban was written for. It also rejected secara lengkap, which the DEFERRED REGISTER already recorded as a sentence the product must be able to say. It was never the lever on the floor rate - the sole style finding on only 3 of 19 floors, and the sole finding of any kind on ZERO.
_removed.style.hedging mungkin: MOVED 2026-08-17 out of this file and into lib/validate/style.js#hedgeAboutReader. Golden rule 7 bans hedging INSIDE A CLAIM, and mungkin in a clause about a THIRD PARTY hedges that party guess, not the claim about her: Orang lain mungkin mengira X, padahal tujuanmu selalu sama is fully committed about her, and it is the salah_dikira shape the hooks are built on. Measured: 14 of 15 mungkin findings had a non-reader subject. cenderung, agak and sepertinya are UNCHANGED and stay here.

verdict._rule: A PAIR READING STATES NO OVERALL VERDICT AND NO SCORE (compat-p4-p5-rules.md 2.4). This list is EMPTY on purpose: the constructions that express a verdict are Indonesian - cocok, tidak cocok, a percentage, a rating - and Reyner is the sole authority on Indonesian register (rule 20). lib/validate/pair.js reads it and logs a FLAG per hit, which cannot fail a reading, so patterns can be fitted against real renders before any of them rejects anything. Adding a pattern here that REJECTS is a gate change: it bumps STAGE6_VERSION in the same commit, alone.
